summary: Turkey Creek Airport is a small remote airfield serving the Aboriginal community of Turkey Creek (Warmun) in the East Kimberley region of Western Australia. It provides essential air access to an isolated area near the famous Bungle Bungle Range and Purnululu National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The airport primarily handles general aviation and charter flights, connecting residents and tourists to larger regional centres like Kununurra and Halls Creek.
faqs:
Q: What is Turkey Creek Airport primarily used for?
A: The airport serves the remote Warmun community and supports tourism traffic heading to Purnululu National Park and the Bungle Bungle Range, as well as general aviation and medical/royal flying doctor services.

Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to Turkey Creek Airport?
A: Scheduled commercial service is very limited; most visitors arrive via charter flights or private aircraft from Kununurra or Halls Creek.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: Facilities are minimal, typical of remote outback strips, with no terminal building. Passengers should arrange ground transport in advance with local accommodation providers.

Q: What is the best time of year to fly to Turkey Creek?
A: The dry season (May to September) is the most popular and reliable period, as the wet season can cause road and sometimes air access disruptions.
transport_tips: Ground transport from the airport is limited, so arrange a pickup with your accommodation or tour operator in advance, as there are no taxis or rideshare services. If arriving by charter from Kununurra, it's roughly a one-hour flight covering about 200 km over rugged Kimberley terrain. The nearby Great Northern Highway connects Turkey Creek to Kununurra and Halls Creek by road for those combining air and 4WD travel.
local_tip: Pack light and bring all your own supplies, including water and snacks, as the closest shops and fuel are in the community itself and stocks can be limited. Early morning or late afternoon flights offer the best chances of scenic views of the Bungle Bungle domes on approach.
